featured_reviews.review_text: Beautiful interior with good ambiance. They have musical nights as Thursday seems Karaoke night. Lots of people to sing. Food is not bad but average. Service is not bad too. Very attentive servers. Street parking only.

featured_reviews.name: Merlyn
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had originally checked with Soul Fry for their karaoke nights, but the owner mentioned that reservations usually need to be made around 10 days to 2 weeks in advance. Later, we ended up going there for lunch on one of the days. I had even called beforehand to ask if reservations were necessary, and he said yes, definitely. But when we actually reached, the restaurant was pretty empty.

The food was good — nothing extremely standout, but overall decent. One thing we did feel though was that everything was slightly on the pricier side for what was offered. That being said, the interiors really give you that old-school Goan tavern vibe, which added a nice charm to the experience.

featured_reviews.name: george joseph
featured_reviews.review_text: What a find. A cute little restaurant with goan vibes right in bandra. You would need to plan to be there around opening time if you want to get a seat in their cozy indoor area. They close for the evening making it a little exclusive with the time restriction. The food was really good. We ordered a chicken starter along with the prawn curry rice and pork vindaloo. The prawn curry rice combo is a must try. Coming from Kerala it gave me those beach vibes. The curry is runny and just perfect with rice. It felt just like it was made at home. The pork was incredible. The pieces they had in the vindaloo consisted of fat and flesh you always die for. Not a lot of places get this right. It was a little too sweet for my usual vindaloo but nonetheless tasty. We could not get an inside sitting spot but consider yourself lucky if you do. I'm sure the experience would be worth it. One of the best places i have visited in bandra.

featured_reviews.name: Ashwinth Naveen
featured_reviews.review_text: My first time in Mumbai, and I have absolutely no regrets choosing Soul Fry as my go-to spot! The karaoke night was an absolute blast and made the whole experience even more memorable. The vibe, music, and overall atmosphere were amazing, and I genuinely had such a great time. Definitely one of the highlights of my trip — would love to visit again!

featured_reviews.name: Marlyn Pereira
featured_reviews.review_text: If you’re into authentic Goan food this is a great place to be. They have karaoke in the evenings and is usually packed so you might have to book in advance, or take only outside seating. The bombil fry and pompfret rechado is a must try.

featured_reviews.name: DS
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is one of my favourite places in Mumbai. They have karaoke nights and also other events happening everyday. When we visited, there was a live music and karaoke night happening. They have a nice variety of cocktails and liquor available. We also tried their prawn rava fry and it was absolutely superb.

It does get extremely crowded on the weekends so getting a table will be difficult. But they let you stand around and order and also have free peanuts. Nice place for seafood.

The crab and bombil were amazing both flavourful and rich - would highly recommend! The seafood biryani was good and the tandoori chicken was moist and delicious. Our only issue with the food today was the mackerel as although the masala was nice the fish itself did not taste as fresh.

featured_reviews.name: Nakul Janglay
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Fresh Catch by Francis recently after hearing a lot about it and honestly came back with mixed feelings.

We tried -

Mushroom Butter Garlic was decent, nothing wrong with it, but nothing memorable either.

Bombil Rava Fry was probably the better dish of the lot. Crispy, tasty, and enjoyable.

Bangda Ambotic Curry was good, but felt like a standard Goan curry. Not something I’d go back specifically for.

Crab Meat Spicy Masala.
It was more like a regular seafood bhurji than a standout crab dish. Now where close to justifying the exorbitant price being charged.

Pomfret Hara Bhara Tawa Fry.
The biggest letdown. The fish didn’t feel particularly fresh, the taste was quite average, and the pricing for a small medium sized portion felt just too steep. For that kind of money (or even less) you can easily get a proper wholesome seafood thali elsewhere.

Overall, the food wasn’t bad, just pretty underwhelming for the pricing and hype. Maybe Goan flavors are intentionally subtler and my palate leans more towards Konkani/Malvani seafood.

If I’m spending that kind of money on seafood in Mumbai, places like Nav Chaitanya and Gajalee still set the benchmark for me in terms of flavor, consistency and value.

featured_reviews.name: Nataleigh Lasrado
featured_reviews.review_text: I visited Fresh Catch on 4 June 2026 and it was excellent!  I asked the bartender to create me a great custom drink and he exceeded my expectations with refreshing and unique creations. My waiter, Lawrence, was extremely helpful in bombil suggestions as well as sourcing from off menu fish. Try Fresh Catch you won’t be disappointed with the drinks, food or service. Ask for Lawrence!

featured_reviews.name: Avinash D'Souza
featured_reviews.review_text: Fresh Catch by Francis is located on the 2nd Floor. Lift available. Had the Prawn pulao and Surmai Rossa Curry with Bombil rava fry. Delicious food and good quality for 2 people

featured_reviews.name: Siddharth Bose
featured_reviews.review_text:
I got to know about this place through YouTube channel Curly Tales, that discusses the favourite food of various celebrities around the country. This place was heavily recommended over the channel by Indian cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar, hence making it easier in terms of choosing the place.

It's a restaurant that serves a vast array of seafood items and some standout dishes that are worthy of being called Legendary.

The dishes I ordered during my visit were Bomblivi fish fry, Prawn Rechada and a bowl of Mixed Sea food pulao.
Add to that, 2 mugs of kingfisher beer to help in aiding the food down the stomach correctly.

The outcome, i was absolutely in wonderland after gorging on their food like there was no tomorrow.

The Prawn Rechada was simply outstanding to another level. The flavours, reminding me of the coastal beaches of India really gave an everlasting taste to hook onto.

The mixed seafood pulao was again another real dish that was crafted amazingly by their chefs. The homemade spice aromas were so imminent that it wasn't a surprise about finishing up the dish by myself.

Overall service and management deserves a 5/5. Food deserves a 5/5 as well .

Keep up the good work.

featured_reviews.name: Vedant Raut (Vedanta)
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Hind Lunch Home,  Pali Naka,  Bandra (west)

Jai Hind is a brightest shining star of the galaxy of coastal cuisine restaurants in Mumbai.  With the few branches spread across the city,  this branch at Bandra,  Pali Naka is their first branch.  The other one is on the Linking Road, which seems to be rather spacious and well furnished.  But as a foodie, my hunt is always for a 'Value for money'  restaurants with excellent quality and quantity and this desire of mime gets fulfilled only in humble homely restaurants.  This branch at Pali Naka has been renovated recently and has only five tables in all.  I recommend to reserve a table in the evening as its a very old and famous restaurant in the area and gets filled quite soon.

The list of dishes we ordered :

1.  Patra Ni Macchi (Basa)
2. Bombil Thali
3. Chicken Sukka Thali

Let me begin with the most yummiest first. The chicken sukka was simply top quality stuff made with supreme perfection. It was creamy with great blend of masalas and literally made us lick our fingers till the end.  The chicken pieces were one of the softest and well marinated ones I ever had.  The Bombil was crispy and crunchy on the outside and soft juicy within. The soul kadi (pink broth)  was thick and made with actual coconut milk.  The texture of the chapatis were homely and rice was soft, fresh and well cooked.

Patra Ni Macchi was steamed to ultimate perfection,  which retained the original flavour of the soft melting Basa fish.  The green stuffing on it was blend of spicy and sour.

Over all,  A must visit restaurant..
Staff is helpful

featured_reviews.name: Pereira Gynel
featured_reviews.review_text:
This place has such an amazing tropical ambience. You are welcomed by soulful Goan music, and the vibe is relaxed and unhurried. The servers don’t rush you, making it a perfect spot to truly enjoy your meal.

Mr. Merwin, the manager, took great care of us, and our servers Sonia and Edwin were humble, polite, and very prompt, obliging us with every request.

The food is unlike anything you’ve tasted.. authentic Goan cuisine rooted deeply in the culture and spices of Goa. Every dish is beautifully presented, with thoughtful plating that elevates the experience without being overdone. The cutlery, plates, and glassware are aesthetically pleasing and enhance the dining experience, without robbing you of quantity. Portions are generous and satisfying.

From the big plates, we had the Traditional Pork Sorpatel with rice, Goan-style chilli chicken, and Surmai fish curry rice. The sorpatel was so authentic it made my mum emotional...it brought back memories of old friends who had cooked traditional pork dishes in her younger days. The Goan-style chilli chicken was the standout dish of the afternoon...smooth, succulent, and packed with a powerful flavour punch. The surmai fish curry rice felt like something an old granny had made, warm, comforting, and soulful.

From the small plates, we tried the Goan fried chicken with spicy mayo...six generous boneless strips, made to order, pairing perfectly with lime and the spicy mayo. The grilled squid stuffed with crab was outstanding, with the masala truly stealing the show. The prawn balchao masala stuffed forminhas crispy tarts were tangy and well-made; while not my personal favourite, they were only overshadowed by stronger dishes. The tender coconut and raw mango salad was light, tropical, refreshing, and beautifully balanced.

For drinks, we had the Coconut Boy Refresher, Kokum Spritz, and Tamarind Trails. These are not your usual cocktails... Goan spices and flavours take centre stage, and an open mind is needed to fully enjoy them.

Coconut Boy truly lives up to its promise of 'fresh' and delivers an experience that transports you straight to Goa. Highly recommended even if you’re simply looking for some relaxed downtime with exceptional food and service.

featured_reviews.name: Everything On A Plate EOAP
featured_reviews.review_text:
AMBIENCE:

Despite being located at a busy intersection, the instant you come inside, you are taken to a tranquil and unexpectedly quiet environment. Amidst the dim lights and décor paying ode to the Goan theme, what we appreciated the most was the ample open space to move around and even dance (which our daughter did multiple times throughout the night).

FOOD:
Vegetable Cheese Rissois: Though the classic Portuguese fried pastry is usually filled with meat, we tried the vegetarian version and were not disappointed. It starts with a crumbly-soft bite which leads to a minced vegetables mixed with cheese that definitely melts in your mouth.

Mapusa Market toast with Cheese & Green Chilli: Coconut boys take on the chilli cheese toast with a twist. On first look it’s just your average cheese chilli toast, but one bite into it and you hit a tangy punch which took us by surprise…. It was mango aachaar! ‘Who would’ave thunk?’ This dish did have some mixed opinions!

Choris Chilli Fry: Choriz tossed with chilli, onion, tomato teamed up with warm, fluffy poee… we absolutely left licking our fingers. Would have gone for round two but there was more to be relished on the menu.

Grilled Squid Stuffed with Crab: A host suggestion that we absolutely jumped at the mention of! Crab meat tossed in Recheado, stuffed into a squid & grilled… a lot of effort goes into this. Hints of spice married with the sweetness of the crab meat and the bite of squid… a messy meal you must try at least once! Definitely big brownie points for the squid NOT being chewy.

Mushroom & vegetables slow cooked with Xacuti masala: A medley of steamed veggies (Mushroom, carrot, potato, cauliflower) tossed in a Xacuti gravy. You have an option of Poee or steamed rice to accompany it and we went with the latter. We requested them to hold back the spice a bit for our toddler & it’s wholesome, earthy, slightly-sweet coconut-ty broth was welcomed with a smack of the lips.

Serradura: This simple pudding can go awry in so many ways… And believe me, we've tasted some absolute disasters. But coconut boy absolutely nailed-it! The crumbly, biscuit dust alternated with fluffy, light whipped cream was what we devoured at the end of a great meal. Not too sweet, not too dense… just perfect.

Service: The service undoubtedly elevated our entire experience! We had Siddhesh giving us amazing recommendations and making sure we had everything we needed. Akbar stopped by with some fantastic banter, and last but not least, Faustin, whom our daughter adored and sat with virtually the entire dinner, allowing us to savour every bite!

SUMMING UP: If you love Goan food, it’s definitely an experience you do not want to miss. Right from the décor to the service, it’s comfy, cozy and warm. The cost is a bit on the higher end but the quality and flavors are worth every penny.

If you are looking for that authentic Mumbai seafood vibe, Jai Jawan in Bandra is pure bliss. Here is a breakdown of a legendary meal:

The Star: Fried Fish with Pav

The Fried Fish here is iconic—perfectly seasoned, crispy on the outside, and flaky within. But the real game-changer is pairing it with the Mumbai Pav. There is something about the texture and flavor of a local Mumbai pav that just hits differently; it’s the ultimate vessel for the spicy fish, especially when you load it up with their signature green chutney and crunchy onions. It’s a simple combination, but it's a "Mumbaikar" soul-food experience

The Sides & Mains
• Prawns Crispy: These lived up to the name. Golden, crunchy, and packed with flavor, they are the perfect appetizer to snack on while you soak in the Bandra energy

• Chicken Tawa Biryani: To wrap things up, the Chicken Tawa Biryani is a must-try. Unlike traditional dum biryanis, the tawa style gives it a unique, rustic smoky flavor and a spice profile that is bold and satisfying.

The Verdict
Eating here isn't just about the food; it's about the "Bliss of Taste." If you want to eat like a true Mumbaikar, grabbing a plate of fish and pav at Jai Jawan is an absolute rite of passage.

Highly Recommended for: Seafood lovers and anyone craving an authentic taste of Mumbai’s street-side culinary excellence.

Small sitting but service is super fast and turn around table is that like always waiting customers in big rush.

All the best team JJ.

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Londhe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Jawan, Bandra

I recently visited Jai Jawan with my friends after a movie, mainly because we had seen and heard a lot about the place through Instagram reels. Since we were already in Bandra, we decided to give it a try. We reached the restaurant around 9:00 PM, which is peak dinner time, and had to wait for nearly 20 minutes to get a table for four—which was understandable considering the rush.

Once seated, we ordered Chicken Tikka Masala and Chicken Tandoori as starters. The starters were okayish in taste, nothing impressive. I assume this might have been due to the restaurant working at full capacity during peak hours.

For the main course, we ordered Butter Chicken with Rumali Rotis. Unfortunately, this was the biggest disappointment of the night. I’ve had butter chicken at countless restaurants, and honestly, this was the worst butter chicken I’ve had so far—lacking flavor, richness, and balance. We also ordered Chicken Fried Rice, which again was just average.

The service experience further added to the disappointment. There was a shortage of waiters, resulting in long waiting times for food. The staff seemed extremely busy and didn’t really have the time to listen properly to customer requests or feedback.

Another thing that stood out negatively was the entertainment setup. The restaurant has two large TV screens, but they were continuously playing the same 5-minute loop video of a Japanese city. On that particular day, there was an India cricket match, and playing it on at least one screen would have kept customers engaged—especially since food service was delayed.

Overall, I personally regret choosing Jai Jawan that night and feel I could have had a better experience elsewhere. This is purely my personal opinion. You may still try it once to form your own view, but my experience was not a good one.

featured_reviews.name: durgesh gawde
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Hind is a gem for seafood lovers, offering an impressive variety of dishes, generous portions, and prices that feel genuinely value-for-money. If you’re someone who appreciates fresh, well-cooked fish without burning a hole in your pocket, this restaurant easily stands out as one of the best options in the city.

One of the first things you notice at Jai Hind is the sheer range on the menu. From classics like Surmai Fry, Bombil Fry, Rawas Curry, and Prawns Koliwada to specials like Crab Masala and Tawa Pomfret, the restaurant ensures there’s something for every seafood enthusiast. What makes the experience even better is that the quality is consistent. The fish is fresh, perfectly marinated, and cooked with authentic coastal flavours that highlight Mumbai’s rich culinary heritage.

Quantity is another major plus. Unlike many seafood places where portions feel small for the price, Jai Hind gives you hearty servings that truly justify every rupee. Whether you order a thali or an à la carte dish, the plates come generously loaded, making it easy to share or enjoy as a filling meal on your own. Their fish thalis, in particular, are a standout—they offer a balanced combination of fried fish, curry, rice, chapati, and sides, making it both wholesome and satisfying.

The pricing is surprisingly reasonable, especially considering the rising cost of seafood in the city. For the quality and quantity provided, the restaurant manages to keep its rates fair, which is a big reason people return. It’s a great place for regular seafood cravings without feeling guilty about overspending.

The ambience is simple, clean, and comfortable—nothing overly fancy, but perfectly suited for a relaxed and enjoyable meal. Service is prompt, friendly, and attentive, with staff who are happy to recommend dishes based on your taste preferences.

featured_reviews.name: saumya poddar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Goh jia Ting - restaurant in bandra, had been on our list for a while, so after a show, we decided to finally give it a try. To be honest, walking into an almost empty restaurant was a little concerning. We were only the second occupied table, and the place remained virtually vacant throughout our visit. Still, we were extremely hungry and the overwhelmingly positive reviews online convinced us to stay and order.

Unfortunately, things went downhill from there.

One of the strangest parts of the evening was the service. At one point, a staff member stood directly in front of our table, watching us eat for an uncomfortably long time. It wasn’t attentive service—it felt intrusive and awkward. She only moved after we specifically requested her to. It genuinely made us uncomfortable, as though we were being monitored rather than hosted.

When I requested disposable chopsticks, the staff said they had them but then handed me what looked like a stranded stirrers and then later confessed that they don’t have disposable chopstick, then why say yes at the first place. Super careless and unprofessional.

The food was even worse. The prawn tempura roll tasted like it had been fried in old, stale oil. Instead of gyoza, we were served something that resembled chicken momos. The lobster roll was completely inedible and was left untouched after a few bites.

The cocktail we ordered, made with star fruit, was equally disappointing. It was so bad that we replaced it with a simple whisky just to avoid any more unpleasant surprises.

After struggling through the starters, we decided not to risk ordering anything else and left for another restaurant to have dinner. The entire experience felt like a complete waste of money.

What started as a restaurant we were genuinely excited to try ended up being one of the most disappointing dining experiences we’ve had in Bandra. Between the awkward service, poor food quality, disappointing drinks, and overall lacklustre experience, we left wondering how the glowing reviews online could possibly reflect what we experienced.

There are far too many great dining options in Bandra to spend your time and money here.

PLEASE DO NOT VISIT, would not recommend at all.

We had a 10:00 PM reservation and were only seated at 11:00 PM after standing inside the restaurant for an hour in complete chaos. What’s the point of making a booking? We ordered black bean veggies but were served some butter garlic gravy that tasted purely of cornstarch — no salt, no flavor, completely inedible. By 11:30 PM we were so hungry and frustrated that we didn’t even bother asking for it to be changed, but it was honestly one of the worst dishes we’ve had.

To top it off, we had to ask for the bill three times, and even then it took 20 minutes. Zero regard for guests’ time.

Completely ruined our evening. When you’re paying premium prices at a so-called upscale restaurant, basic service, organization, and edible food should not be too much to expect. Would not recommend.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Veranda around 4 PM, and the first thing to note is that the kitchen was partially closed at that time, which limited a few options. Still, we managed to order a decent variety of dishes.
We tried prawns thecha, chicken 65, chicken tenders, pizza, pasta, and Hakka noodles. Most of the food was actually good and enjoyable. The highlight of the meal was definitely the prawns thecha, easily the best dish on the table. It was flavorful, well-cooked, and something I’d genuinely go back for.
The pizza and pasta were nice, chicken 65 was solid, and overall the food quality was pretty satisfying. But the Hakka noodles were a letdown. They had a strong smell, likely from the egg and chicken, which made it hard to enjoy the dish.
Another downside was the timing of the chicken tenders. They arrived way too late, almost after we were done eating everything else, which kind of ruined the flow of the meal.
That said, the ambience is where Veranda really stands out. The place looks amazing, has a great vibe, and the location is perfect for a chill outing in Bandra.
Overall, it’s a good place with great ambience and mostly good food, but a few issues with timing and consistency in dishes hold it back slightly.

Food:
Good, guilty and gluttonous North Indian food is served with love on brass cutlery. You feel the butter in every bite. Quality is great, though quantity is frequently insufficient for a couple of people. Earlier they used to include dal makhani and dahi etc. with their mouthwatering kulchas and parathas but now they have stopped doing that. Tandoori Starters and tandoor breads are must try for.
Service: servers are frank and friendly and a bit too nosy sometimes.
Ambience: small place, but they made max out of it. They transfer you to dhaba instantly.
Value for money: This would disappoint you, as for what they ask for; their quantity is too little. Hope they work on their quantity.
A highly recommended place for small group or family to visit if you are craving some good Kulchas, Parathas, Tandooris and a glass full of lassi.

Imagine a dhaba in the middle of the city and that too in Bandra!! Well got an opportunity to visit “ Papa Pancho da Dhaba” with family. Was surprised on a Thursday night, it was crowded with people waiting to be seated, that is how popular the place is.

We ordered the Tandoori Chicken which was crisp from outside and moist from inside, well spiced and really tasty.  Next was Dahi Pappi Chat, a well balanced crispy, chatpata, khatta meetha, but for the cost, the quantity could be a lil more.

In main course it was Chicken Handi with Butter Garlic Naan, served with Dal Makhni and Curd. Next was but for sure Amritsari Kulcha…. served with white butter dollop and buttery dal makhni. We were almost full, but on suggestion we ordered Chicken Dal Khichadi, which surprisingly was very comforting with bits of Chicken … we ended the meal with  Lassi… a must at any Punjabi place. A huge copper glass full!!

If u come at Carter Road Promenade or Joggers Park on Friday, Saturday n Sunday evenings, don't go to opposite Khau Galli, rather gift your taste buds a homely savoury treat here. Can get home parcels too.
Located at Carter Road Promenade end, at Khar Danda, this cluster of 7-8 sea food eatery stalls is a luscious place overseeing stone beach. Can get romantic in full moon nights if ambience is made more clean by BMC n locals.
Run by local fishermen community women, u can taste homely fish/ prawns/ crabs flavours in their traditional spices.
Slightly congested to eat in-situ, but its OK. Please don't litter in the sea as it is narrow promenade part only.
Opens in evenings of Friday, Saturday n Sunday till 12 midnight.

customer_updates.text: Absolutely loved the surmai thali, the gravy was also good and chicken gharghuti masala was also amazing. Food for 2 came to around 2000rs.

featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this place with my ex-colleagues, and to be honest, The vibe of the place is great for spending time with family.

We ordered quite a few dishes including prawns masala fry, bombil masala, bombil rawa fry, grilled pomfret, crab lollipop, chicken, and finally prawns biryani.

Talking about the food, the crab lollipop was interesting. It obviously felt like frozen food, but the taste was still good. However, most of the seafood dishes were a little disappointing for us. The fish dishes were not spicy enough and lacked that strong flavor we were expecting. The stuffed pomfret was just okay-okay and felt more like boiled fish rather than properly fried.

We also ordered a chicken dish and specifically requested it to be spicy, but unfortunately, it turned out a bit sweet, and none of us really liked it.

But the highlight of the meal was definitely the prawns biryani. It was really, really good and honestly the best dish we had there.

Overall, the ambience and company made the experience enjoyable, but food-wise, only a few dishes really stood out for us.

featured_reviews.name: hemali kantharia
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our go-to family dinner spot for any and every occasion. From small celebrations to casual dinners, this place has always been our first choice. Over time we’ve tried almost everything on the menu, and every visit somehow turns into another food memory with family.

If there are two dishes I would recommend to anyone visiting, it has to be the Bombil Fry and Peri Peri Bombil. They are easily my brother’s and my absolute favourites perfectly crispy, full of flavour, and something we end up ordering almost every single time.

And no meal here feels complete without the Kokum Sarbat or Kokum Soda. That refreshing, tangy punch of flavour just balances the seafood so well and makes the whole experience even better.

Good food, great flavours, and the comfort of family dinners this place truly feels special to us. Easily one of the best seafood restaurants and definitely a spot we’ll keep coming back to.

featured_reviews.name: Mitesh Parmar
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was the final restaurant I attended on my trip and a great place to end on.

Unfortunately at the time of our attendance the A/C was not in working order which the manager/owner advised on prior to entering, however we still went in as they had fans going on.

Didn't plan to eat a lot but to take in the delights on offer as again this was a place recommended.

We were given good information by the manager on some of the dishes and on ordering the food arrived after a short time. temperatures were on point and flavours were amazing. The prawn starters were so good, especially the Prawns Garlic Butter, so much so we ordered another tray. I also order the Mutton Chops Ghee Roast and as it sat in front of me my mouth was watering. Spice level on this was perfect, had a nice little kick but was really enjoyable and not in a overpowering way. I found that the chop may have been slightly overdone to my liking, however this didn't take the enjoyment away from it.

The meals ordered were enjoyed by everyone in the party which also included children (they really enjoyed the Prawns Garlic Butter). Pricing of the meals and overall was very reasonable and this place is worth a visit if you have never been. I will look to return here again if I visit Mumbai again.

featured_reviews.name: Kairo
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had lunch on Sunday. We were 5 people and it was an amazing experience. The food quality and taste both were top notch. We had order chicken and mutton thalis along with other dishes. We liked all of it. Especially Rucha ma'am was very friendly and asked us whether we like like our food. Tho service was a little slow, She was happy to help us and welcoming too.
Would recommend this place if ur fond of non veg food

featured_reviews.name: Hitesh Harisinghani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Nav Kayastha Pangat on a Sunday night and had a great experience. We waited around 10 minutes for a table, and the ambience along with the friendly staff made us feel comfortable right away. The warm Kokum drink is a perfect way to welcome guests!

What we ordered:

Mutton Kheema Pattice: A deep-fried snack with mutton kheema stuffed in mashed potato – absolutely delicious!

Bharleli Bombil: Bombil fish stuffed with green chutney and fried. Tasty, but next time I’d prefer plain bombil with chutney on the side.

Tisrya Kalwan: A unique and flavorful clams gravy that paired perfectly with wade.

The total bill for two came to ₹1400. Prices are on the higher side, but the menu is full of interesting and authentic CKP veg/non-veg dishes. Was this the best Mahrashtrian cuisine? No, not really but it's worth trying!

In a very long time, I wasn’t filled with such a subtle and home-blend restaurant. Calling it a restaurant might be over exaggerating because this place is run by a family and the authentic Goan food that they serve just makes you feel at home. This charming place is nestled right beside the highway, amidst a small colony of homes. It’s seamlessly blended in, creating an atmosphere that feels more like a family’s home than a resting place.
We have got the Surmai Fish Curry Thali and the classic Chicken Masala Thali. Both were just amazing and homely to taste.

Their staffs are very friendly and sweet enough that you feel like home.

While the quantity of food didn’t quite match the pricing, the quality was great.

This is very good place to recommend for a family lunch/dinner. I am sure you won’t be disappointed with it. Enjoy.

featured_reviews.name: Javed Akhtar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Here’s a full review in your signature tone, covering the Torii experience:

⸻

Torii, Bandra – Big on Vibe, Big on Bill, Bigger on Taste

When your group of diners ranges from sushi scholars to soy sauce dabblers, you need a place that checks all boxes. Torii in Bandra came highly recommended—and spoiler alert—it almost lives up to the hype, and then some.

Let’s start from the outside: that black-and-white arched entrance with the gold-lettered TORII feels like you’re about to enter a movie set. Inside, the vibe is unmistakably plush—with mirrored ceilings, retro lampshades, opulent seating, and music that doesn’t scream at you but keeps the energy flowing. It’s where Japanese zen meets Mumbai glam.

The Meal
We were 7. The table bill read ₹45,999, so yes, about ₹6.5K per head after taxes and service, but here’s what made it feel worth it:
•	Cold Young Coconut Carpaccio – Sounds fancy and tasted the part. Light, tropical, and a perfect start.
•	Miso Black Cod – Showstopper dish. Silky, melt-in-mouth. It’s what black cod dreams are made of.
•	Chicken Chilli Oil & Lemongrass Chicken Tsukune – Packed flavour bombs. The chilli oil was a standout.
•	Cold Prawns Tempura Maki – Crisp, clean, and a hit with everyone at the table.
•	Twilight Tingles (mocktail) – Refreshing and not sugary, a tough balance to nail.
•	Torii X-mess Sundae – The name may be cheeky, but this dessert brought childlike joy with its waffle castle presentation. The kind of ending you photograph before devouring.

Service
Smooth, attentive, and non-intrusive. Our server knew the menu well and paced the meal right. That’s half the job done in high-end dining.

What Could Be Better?
Not much honestly. A couple of small hits and misses on portion sizes (looking at you, gyoza), but hey, we weren’t here for the quantity.
The bill might jolt you for a second, but by the end of the night, you’ll justify it to yourself with, “Well, the black cod made up for it.”

My final two bit

Paise gaye, par taste ban gaya.

Aide  dessert  pe toh calories bhi selfie mangti hai.

📍 Final Verdict:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ — A strong 5 stars for a place that brings together design, service, and standout dishes under one gilded roof. For special dinners, date nights, or flex-worthy Instagram reels, Torii hits the spot..

featured_reviews.name: Dr Arvind Yadav
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Hidden Gem for Konkani Food Lovers!

The atmosphere at The Konkani Haven – Isvara Restaurant is truly something special — calm, serene, and perfect for a relaxed meal. The ambiance sets the tone with soothing music, tasteful decor, and a peaceful vibe that immediately makes you feel at home.

The food is the real star here — authentic Konkani flavors that are hard to find elsewhere. Every dish we tried was fresh, flavorful, and clearly made with care. The seafood options, in particular, were outstanding!

Service was warm and attentive without being intrusive. You can tell the staff genuinely care about your dining experience.

Highly recommend for anyone looking to enjoy great food in a tranquil setting. Will definitely be coming back!

featured_reviews.review_text:

We also had the stuffed pomfret which was a misnomer because it was actually patrani maach... nevertheless it was fresh so no complaints there...
What was disappointing was their bombil fry and their mandeli fry.... unfortunately what they served us was charred bombil...not at all expected from a seafood speciality restaurant.
Their solkadi is good...but I think u should go for their innovative cocktails...we had the Aampanna gimlet which was refreshing!
We had been to the restaurant in the afternoon and there was only one person who took care of everything...maybe noone goes there in the afternoon...so I would advise go there only for dinner when u would b able to enjoy the ambience as well cause without the lighting...the place is not worth spending ur time in.

Can go once though..cause the seafood is fresh and the masalas they prepare in are different and tasteful.

featured_reviews.name: Barnali Bose
featured_reviews.review_text:
The food is delicious, no-nonsense good. The Dragon roll sushi is fresh and tasty, the Hamachi with Ponzo could be better. The pork belly bao is soft, the meat tender, and the flavour, spot-on. The spicy prawn Donburi is a burst of smoky spicy flavours and the mini pork ramen, just as comforting as a ramen should be with 2 large strips of pork. Both, highly recommended! The Hazelnut cacao was the perfect sweet n salty dessert to wrap up the meal.

I would have given them 5*, but for two things. One, they try to fill up the ground floor and misrepresent facts about the AC malfunctioning on the 1st floor. And even if you feel uncomfortable (which I did), they will not let you move to a better table. We went in early, yet were made to sit in a cramped corner beside the bar and washroom which made it quite noisy and not the best seats. This was our second visit, and on both occasions the restaurant acted out with the seating
Second, you are on the Conde Nast list, the basic serving etiquette that is expected is that you don’t pile all the food together on the table. One can ask the patron whether everything is expected in one go or simply bring the food as different courses. Sadly, not at Mizu!

featured_reviews.name: Prakash Dhalwani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mizu has quickly become one of my favorite spots in Bombay. The vibe is super calming and minimal, with a beautiful setup that makes you want to just sit back and enjoy a long, relaxed meal.

We ordered the salmon roll, prawn sushi, asparagus sushi, and both chicken and veg gyoza—and honestly, everything was incredible. The salmon roll was so fresh and perfectly balanced, and the prawn sushi had just the right amount of flavor without being overpowering. Even the asparagus sushi (which I wasn’t expecting much from) turned out to be a standout—super clean and fresh-tasting.

The gyozas were spot on too—crispy on the bottom, juicy inside, and served with a dipping sauce that really tied it all together. You can tell they really care about the quality of ingredients and presentation.

Drinks were great (highly recommend trying one of their signature cocktails), and the service was warm and helpful without hovering. It’s definitely on the pricier side, but for the quality of food, the ambiance, and the overall experience, I’d say it’s totally worth it.

Already looking forward to going back!

featured_reviews.name: TheLefty Prodigy
featured_reviews.review_text: I had such an amazing experience. Everything from the sushis to ramen was top notch. Loved the pork broth, the katsu chicken rolls, the chicken gyoza, the non-alcoholic cocktails and the desserts! Especially the desserts! The server was Joshua who was exceptional! Always smiling and super friendly. ❤️

featured_reviews.name: Swati Pillai
featured_reviews.review_text:
Overpriced, overhyped, and shockingly arrogant

Mizu is sold as a top luxury restaurant in Mumbai, with visits from celebrities and the affluent, but the experience last night was a complete letdown.

Even the interiors felt like a missed opportunity, far from the polished, premium vibe the pricing suggests.

We spent ₹17,600+ on small plates and drinks, and most of the food was average at best, nothing you wouldn’t get at a regular Asian restaurant.

The service was HORRENDOUS.
We were warned three times before arriving that we must vacate the table by 9:30 PM, and then reminded multiple times again during dinner. It felt like we were being rushed out from the moment we sat down.

Service was slow and sloppy, and we had to constantly ask them to clear used plates and bowls. They even forgot our order. We were even asked repeatedly to return the menu, as if they don’t have enough menus to run a “premium” restaurant.

The most unbelievable part: when my friend considered ordering another glass of wine, the steward (Vijay) actually said, “It’s better you don’t order.”

For a place charging these prices, the attitude is unacceptable. The service is abysmal.
Mizu cares more about table turnover than hospitality. What makes such places arrogant in an Indian city with a culture that is driven with hospitality and warmth?
Never again, Mizu. I’m taking my hard-earned money where the service, atmosphere, food quality, and overall experience is commensurate!

featured_reviews.name: JASON SEQUEIRA
featured_reviews.review_text:
🍣 Mizu – Bandra Review 🍜

Had an amazing dining experience at Mizu Bandra, one of those places that perfectly blends cozy vibes with top-notch Japanese cuisine. The ambiance is modern, minimal, and effortlessly elegant — perfect for both a casual outing or a special dinner. ✨

Here’s what I tried:

🍣 Salmon and Prawn Rolls – absolutely fresh and flavorful! The rolls were perfectly rolled, with the right balance of rice, seafood, and seasoning. The texture was spot on, and every bite just melted in the mouth. Easily one of the highlights of the meal!

🥟 Gyozas – crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside. These dumplings were packed with flavor and served hot, making them the perfect appetizer.

🍜 Ramen – rich, flavorful, and comforting. The broth was hearty and aromatic, the noodles cooked just right, and the toppings perfectly balanced — truly authentic and satisfying.

🍛 Golden Curry – such a comforting dish! Creamy, flavorful, and mildly spiced with that signature Japanese curry richness. It’s the kind of dish that just warms you up instantly.

🍗 Chicken Rice Bowl – tender, well-marinated chicken served over fluffy rice — simple, hearty, and full of flavor. Perfect for anyone who loves balanced, wholesome bowls.

Everything at Mizu was beautifully presented and tasted even better than it looked. The service was friendly and attentive, adding to the overall experience. If you’re in Bandra and craving authentic Japanese flavors with a modern twist, Mizu is definitely the place to go.

featured_reviews.name: Mita Biswas
featured_reviews.review_text: Easily one of the best Japanese dining experiences in Mumbai! The ramen broth here is incredibly rich and comforting, absolute perfection. The vibe is lively and sophisticated, making it an amazing spot for a special night out. The staff was incredibly warm and helpful with recommendations. Don't skip dessert; the Japanese cheesecake is a must! Make sure to book a table well in advance.

The place feels a bit overpriced considering the overall ambiance and portion sizes. Still, if you’re in the area and craving some pan-Asian flavors, it’s worth a visit — just be ready for a slightly premium bill.

featured_reviews.name: Pratik K. Mody
featured_reviews.review_text:
Nom Nom is such a vibe!

The ambience really stands out! That warm, dim lighting sets the perfect mood for an intimate dinner without feeling too “try-hard.” It’s the kind of place where you naturally slow down, settle in, and actually enjoy the evening.
The food, overall, was really good and definitely amps up the experience. That said, I’d love to see a wider variety of sushi and noodle dishes on the menu. The bao bun was a bit on the chewy side, and the filling-to-bun ratio felt slightly off (could’ve used more filling). The silken tofu, though was an absolute standout. It genuinely melted in the mouth and was a wow dish, even if I wish the portion was a little more generous. The peach iced tea was perfect. Dessert-wise, the mango sticky rice could’ve been better, it felt a bit like mango purée with pieces and rice, missing that coconut-y flavour and crunch (both of which are not very difficult to crack).
Definitely a spot I’d come back to (and happily recommend) when I’m in the mood for a relaxed, date-night style dinner.

featured_reviews.name: Sandeep Damle
featured_reviews.review_text: Went here on a Sunday for lunch without any reservation, and we immediately got seating by the live sushi counter, which was surprisingly cozy. The ambience of the place is simple but pretty, just how a japanese restaurant should be. We tried a sushi, gyoza, yakitori chicken and udon noodles, and although everything tasted great, nothing really stood out as outstanding. The thing is that these days there are several multi-cuisine/asian restaurants who also serve good authentic japanese dishes, which thus reduces the novelty factor of an authentic japanese-only restaurant, although the menu is wider here. The service here is excellent, and the prices are also reasonable. Valet parking is available. Overall there's no negative about the place and it's definitely worth visiting.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellent Ramen. Service was average. And decor was good and minimal.
What mattered was what we went for - Soul food and got that. Ordered 3 different ramen and all were excellent. The pork and chicken broth were better than the vegetarian one.
We just walked in and got a table without an issue. Reservation was not done as the numbers were always engaged which we tried for last 3 days.

featured_reviews.name: Indrajit Advani
featured_reviews.review_text: Having visited Kuuraku a week earlier, this was the second Japanese restaurant in Mumbai to positively surprise us. The smoked crispy pork belly was not too salty (as is often the case with pork in India) and it was indeed tender though it was a shame that it was doused in mayonnaise. The rock shrimp and squid tempura was a generous portion though the batter was just a little too heavy and somewhat disguised the taste of the prawn and squid. We had a prawn okomiyaki, which was very enjoyable though I would have liked to have the option of no bonito flakes, and a little less sauce, that again disguised the taste of the pancake. The chicken tsukune was perfect and one of the highlights of the meal, perhaps bettered only by the buta burra with enoki mushroom, which was divine. The spider roll was another generous portion item and quite good again. Having enjoyed the food so much we went full blast and ordered one desser each. The black sesame ice cream was pretty good without perhaps the subtle flavour of some of the best that we've had but it was certainly better than the warabi mochi, which was a limp disappointment. But the hit of the three was definitely the fuji tropica. Once it arrived we didn't know what to expect - but it was fantastic - reminding us of 'dippin' dots'. All in all a very enjoyable meal although at RS8,700 it wasn't cheap.

featured_reviews.name: Sav
featured_reviews.review_text:
I crave for authentic japnese restaurants with fresh high quality meat and in one line, this is it. The food was absolutely the best authentic quality of japanese one could hope to get in India. It was not perfect by any means yet I could not ask for more considering how atrocious some other places can be.
The cocktails were all for a sweet pallet but the match foam was incredible, a delicacy. The Katsu curry, which I have tried many of was most certainly one of the best. I know now that everytime I travel to Bombay, I shall come by here to feast.

Wine menu could be improved for by glass for such a restaurant.

featured_reviews.review_text: Sadicha Restaurant at MIG Club, Bandra serves a satisfying chicken thali with authentic homemade flavors. The curry is well-spiced, portions are filling, and service is quick. Simple ambiance, good value for money, and a comforting meal overall.

featured_reviews.name: Shyam Singh
featured_reviews.review_text: They have been serving delicious Maharashtrian food for over a decade now. It’s open only during lunch and dinner time. Prawns fry and Chicken sukha is a must try. Vegetarian options are as good as none.

featured_reviews.name: Manoj Arkar
featured_reviews.review_text: The food has no taste at all, how can you eat Malvani style food? A person should be satisfied after tasting the food. Their food is for show and the Solakdi should not be drunk. It tasted like water. The money was totally wasted.

featured_reviews.name: Ankita Mukul Das
featured_reviews.review_text:
Got to know about this place via Google as I was in BKC and wanted to eat fish, looking at the rating I thought of visiting this place.
The place is quite small and gives homely feeling, looking at this i got happy thinking the food would be really nice and homemade.
We ordered for a chicken thali, a pomfret thali and an surmai thali and a tisrya sukkah.
Was totally disappointed when the food came, the tisrya sukkha seemed like tisrya masala and was very sweet. The surmai thali was not upto the mark, surmai was very small, I have never had such small piece of surmai in any of the fish outlet.
Quantity wise I was totally disappointed, chicken thali had just 2 pieces of chicken.
Sol kadhi seemed to be like water added to it, we had reached around 2:30-2:45pm and I think we were served the left over food as it was closing time.
I will not recommend this restaurant to anyone, specially who is a fish lover.

featured_reviews.name: Ashish Amrute
featured_reviews.review_text:
In Mumbai, people are often misguided into thinking Mangalorean or Goan Cuisine as Malvani.. But not here…!!

So I came here today with a friend. He ordered a Tisrya (Clams) Thali and I called for Mori (Shark) Thali. Both were excellent. The fish was fresh and the gravy was very tasty and perfectly spiced. The quantity in each thali was perfect for one adult. If at all I have to complain then I would say, I missed the small portion of Suka Jawla (dry baby shrimp) that is also served as part of the seafood thali in my town.

The service was prompt and the staff was welcoming. Hygiene is taken care of. The place is tiny and very modestly done up, so if you value the ambience as much as your food, then this isn't the place for you. Free Street Parking is available.

If you are craving for good authentic Malvani Food… Sadichha is just the place for you.

featured_reviews.name: Deepthi Nair
featured_reviews.review_text: What a find this place. It's located just opp the MIG club...it's a quaint tiny lil place..serving seafood like a boss! We ordered everything and lived everything. The bombil fry, prawns, mandeli, the pomfret stuffed with prawns (awesomeness) and all the thalis..we had prawn, mory, clams, surmai and pomfret thalis..and for vegetarians with us they specially made some pithala and a good veg thali :). Highly recommend!

featured_reviews.name: nirant palav
featured_reviews.review_text: It was a really great restaurant for sea food, Chicken Masala was so tasty, Mutton was well cooked and Bombil/Bombay Duck fry was an amazing must try dish if you visit the hotel, Do visit the Hotel for Just Bombil/Bombay Duck fry Really great taste and crispy

featured_reviews.name: S F
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was a favourite joint especially since our office was in bkc.
However my last visit was nothing short of a huge disappointment.
Menu has changed and even bombil is priced APS which is silly since bombil is not a premium fish . I paid 360 for a plate... Received burnt oily bombil... Not worth it.
The sol kadhi was watery, coconut milk seemed split.. no basic garnish of coriander and no taste of any spice..
Pics attached. This was a parcel pickup.
Avoid visiting.. these guys need to check what their chefs are doing.

featured_reviews.name: Savio Dcunha
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visit this eatery if the rain caught you off guard when you were strolling near St. Teresa Church. You can sample delicious chicken, prawn, and dim sum dishes. Start your lunch with a delicious cup of tea. A very tiny interior room upstairs and a couple of outdoor tables in a very tiny space.

Here, the staff is reputed to be polite. At Zao Cha House, the customer service is excellent. There are rumours of reduced prices here. Customers are drawn in by the pleasant environment. The location is adorable and well-kept; it's a tiny room with a few outdoor tables and an upper room. Service was prompt and courteous. Good food with basic, distinct flavour. Numerous vegan and vegetarian choices.

At Zao Cha House, two people would pay around 1800. No, alcohol is not served at Zao Cha House. That's unfortunate. There is valet parking available at Zao Cha House, however it can be challenging to accommodate your car in the narrow byways surrounding the establishment, so allow an extra 15 minutes.

Pan Asian cuisine is the primary food offered at Zao Cha House.

We had already tried these dishes and was lovely:
Suimai Chicken, Prawns, Chive Squid, and Salt and Pepper
Seafood, Claypot Chicken, and Roast Lamb, Green Tea (Flavoured), Sea Food YangCol  and the Truffle Pastry

Overall a 3/5 for the lack of space, parking challenges and non-alcoholic menu options.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Zao Cha House 💖

featured_reviews.name: Sameer Sanghvi
featured_reviews.review_text: The place is super! Dumplings are definitely the stand out dish. We had a lot of dumplings different varieties,, but i liked the prawn dumplings the best. Had soup and noodles which was part of their all you can eat dim sum n tea lunch! Must visit!

featured_reviews.name: Cherry
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently had the pleasure of dining at Zao Cha House, a Pan-Asian restaurant in the heart of Mumbai city  .From the moment I walked in, I was impressed by the sleek and modern decor, which was a perfect contrast to the traditional flavors that awaited me.

The menu was extensive and featured a variety of dishes from across Asia. I started with the Petrichor and Yumcha iced tea for drinks, which was really refreshing, perfect way to kickstart lunch. For appetizers we chose Chicken Xialong, soft bao on the outside and hot soup on the inside. Next, we had the Prawns Cheung, this is now a personal favourite .The last starter we chose was Chicken Suimai, if you enjoy soft, juicy dimsums...this is for you. For my main course, I ordered the Yang chow rice with Chicken Macadamia, which was really cooked to perfection and was super flavorful. We chose their chocolate Bao for dessert, it was really fresh and oozing with a mixture of chocolate and nutella. We ended our fulfilling lunch with their Rose Petal and Hibiscus tea which promotes healthy digestion and was the perfect end to a satisfactory meal.

The service was great, with the staff being friendly and attentive throughout my meal. They were able to provide great recommendations on what to order, and I appreciated how they checked in on me periodically.

Overall, I would highly recommend Zao Cha House to anyone looking for a great Pan-Asian luxury dining experience in Bandra.The quality of the food and the excellent service makes this restaurant stand out, and I can't wait to go back and try more dishes on the menu.

featured_reviews.name: Siddharth Patkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
An interesting place with some palatable cuisine. The crunchy avocado roll, wasabi prawns, sticky rice in lotus leaf are really delectable and my favourites. The restaurant also serves Chinese tea, which may be paired with some of the dishes. Ask the one serving you for the recommendation or just check the menu where the same will be mentioned.
For those who seek something discerning in South East Asian cuisine, Zao Cha House is a must try.

featured_reviews.name: Jaanya M
featured_reviews.review_text: If you're looking for a delightful restaurant experience in Bandra, Zao Cha House is an excellent choice. From the moment you step inside, the ambiance is warm and inviting, and the service is top-notch. The Rose Petal and Hibiscus Tea is a must-try - it's fragrant and flavorful, and the perfect way to start your meal. The Chicken Xoiaolong Bao and Prawns Cheung are both delicious and expertly crafted, and the Chicken Suimai is simply outstanding. For drinks, the Petrichor and Yumcha Iced Tea are both refreshing and unique. Moving on to the mains, the Yong Chow Rice with Chicken Macadamia is a standout - the flavors are perfectly balanced, and the dish is generously portioned. Finally, the Chocolate Bao for dessert is an absolute must-try - it's rich, decadent, and the perfect end to a fantastic meal. Overall, Zao Cha House is a gem of a restaurant that's definitely worth visiting.

featured_reviews.name: Heliana Mano
featured_reviews.review_text:
So glad we finally tried Zao Cha House. Place is cute and neat - very small space with couple outside tables and a small indoor area upstairs. A kind suggestion to opt out of the perfume-y smell (perhaps air freshener? ) inside as it was very annoying so we opted to sit out mainly because of it.

Service was professional and prompt.

Menu is lovely and food is delicious - reminded us the dim sum we used to have in Chinatowns in the US.

We shared:
- chicken xiao long bao
- chicken prawn xo sauce
- fried turnip cake
- crispy prawn cheung fun
- pan fried lamb dumpling
- crispy duck roll
- spinach roll waterchestnut in black bean sauce
- prawn and chive dumpling
- chamomile tea

Food was amazing - simple clear flavours. Lots of veggie and vegan options too!

Chicken xiao long bao was delicious - the soup was too good, probably the best we have tried here in India so far. My favorites were definitely the latter along with crispy duck, prawn and chive, crispy prawn cheung fun and spinach roll which was very interesting and so innovative. My hubby absolutely loved the pan fried lamb dumpling. The turnip was lovely and very different (more authentic) than other places which fry it too much in my opinion.

Chamomile tea was lovely, though i would have preferred the option of jasmine tea which is my old time favorite with dimsum. Would have loved to see an option of the steamed custard bun that we have always enjoyed in many dim sum places  - I hope to see this on the menu if possible :)

A lovely place. Can't wait to come here again with family and friends :)

featured_reviews.name: Ray (Raymundo)
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dining at Hakkasan Mumbai was a fantastic experience. Every dish we ordered was of exceptional quality, with the tofu dishes standing out in particular — an amazing option for both vegetarians and meat eaters alike. The pomfret fish stir fry was especially flavourful and absolutely delicious.

The highlight of the evening was the outstanding service. The staff managed the sharing dishes seamlessly and were attentive throughout the meal. Chef Raymond Wong personally came to our table for a chat, which was a lovely and memorable touch. Highly recommend — it truly lives up to the Hakkasan reputation.

featured_reviews.name: Anita Aikara
featured_reviews.review_text: Loved the place and the vibes. Was there for the special Chinese New Year menu and the drinks were very good but the food was a standout. The chicken and Chinese cabbage dimsum to the the golden seafood dumplings were exceptional. I enjoyed the Golden Stallion dessert and the prawns wok as well. The sea bass with the crispy skin and scrambled egg on top was quite an enjoyable treat.

featured_reviews.name: Navin
featured_reviews.review_text: Great place and fantastic service. Tried their veg and non-veg dishes. Both were good. Stir fry chicken and chicken spicy dumplings were the best. Try their 5 rice chilli combo, superb! That too veg. Place is great for a small group. Do book in advance.

featured_reviews.name: Ayushi Sancheti
featured_reviews.review_text:
Would 10/10 recommend this especially for a date. The food is authentic chinese and really yum.
The ambiance is luxe, I personally prefer the area near the bar.
Chef Raymond is a great host & super passionate which makes the food taste even nicer.

featured_reviews.name: Susmita Hegde
featured_reviews.review_text: I had a fantastic lunch at Hakkasan—the food and service were top-notch. Dhananjay gave us excellent service.We started with the Spicy Chicken Dumplings (a must-try—super flavorful and spicy; we had them twice). Next came the tender Stir Fry Chicken. The Peach Passion drink was perfectly tangy. We finished with the 5 Style Stir Rice with Chilli Combo, packed with great textures and flavors.Hakkasan nails fine Cantonese dining. Highly recommend!

featured_reviews.name: Joe N
featured_reviews.review_text: An  authentic Cantonese dining experience. Food was amazing, the atmosphere was great and the staff were very friendly and polite. Excellent dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Chirag Patel
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently revisited this upscale Chinese restaurant for brunch, despite previous underwhelming experiences. Unfortunately, the lack of natural light and overuse of tacky blue lights remained a major turnoff. The ambiance, while appealing to some, doesn’t  resonate with me.
The food, while reasonably priced during brunch, didn't change my opinion about Chinese cuisine in Bombay. It still feels like a generic Chinese restaurant in a five-star hotel.

On a positive note, the staff was attentive and well-trained, with noticeably more staff members on deck. The addition of a smoking cabin upstairs was convenient, and the toned-down music was a welcome change. The unlimited flow of good brand cocktails was a great value.

While this restaurant still isn't my favorite, I appreciate the positive changes in price, smoking area, and music volume.

featured_reviews.name: Josef Schneider
featured_reviews.review_text: So glad I booked Hakkasan for my birthday dinner. The food was amazing, especially the Peking duck. The service was friendly and attentive, and I appreciated the excellent recommendations. I'll definitely be coming back here for special occasions.
